 Fils vs Jodar and Zverev vs Shelton – Nitto ATP Finals Predictions
 Written by: Stefan Jonsson | November 17, 2026 
 It’s day three at the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin, here’s a preview for today’s matches in the John McEnroe Group, Arthur Fils vs. Rafael Jodar and Alexander Zverev vs. Ben Shelton, with our betting predictions and odds.
 Arthur Fils vs Rafael Jodar
 This is a must-win match for both debutants. They both lost their openers, so the loser will be 0-2 and all but out of the semifinals. Fils lost to Shelton 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 on Sunday, coming back to level the match after losing the first set but conceding an early break in the decider. He stayed upbeat afterwards, saying he was “not sad” and that he’s already focused on Tuesday. Jodar lost to Zverev 6-4, 6-4, having had two break points when Zverev served for the first set at 5-4. He said the match came down to small details and that it will help him get used to the court.
 Both come into Turin on the back of strong seasons. Fils, the sixth seed, won his first Masters 1000 title in Cincinnati and became the first Frenchman to qualify for the Finals since Gael Monfils in 2016. Jodar, who is 20, is in his first full season on the ATP Tour, and has surged from outside the top 150 to the top 10.
 Jodar leads the head-to-head 2-1, with all three meetings coming this year. Both of Jodar’s wins came on hard courts, in straight sets.
 Predictions and best bets
 Jodar has beaten Fils twice on hard-courts and enter as slight favorite. I will go against the bookies though and predict a hard-fought win for Fils as he has looked slightly better on this surface recently.
 My bet: Fils to win in three sets, at odds 4.20 or +320 (US).
 Alexander Zverev vs Ben Shelton
 Zverev started in impressive form on Sunday. The top seed and world No. 1, who is chasing a third ATP Finals title after winning in 2018 and 2021, beat Jodar 6-4, 6-4 in 1 hour and 28 minutes, holding all ten of his service games, hitting ten aces and not facing a break point in the second set. The German won the US Open this year, beating Shelton in the final.
 Shelton won his first Finals match on Sunday after going winless in Turin last year, edging Fils in three sets. He had a good season, with four titles including Montreal and a first Grand Slam final at the US Open, and he was the runner-up in Paris last week, when he lost to Carlos Alcaraz. Now he faces the player who has beaten him in all six of their meetings.
 Zverev leads the head-to-head 6-0, and he’s 13-2 in sets and 5-0 in tiebreaks. He beat Shelton in the Munich final in 2025, 6-2, 6-4, in straight sets at the ATP Finals last year, and in the US Open final in September, 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2.
 Predictions and best bets
 Shelton’s serve gives him a chance against anyone, and he took a set off Zverev in the US Open final. But the new World no 1 is almost impossible to break when he serves like he did on Sunday, especially on these courts. He has won every one of their tiebreaks, and Shelton hasn’t been able to find a way past him in six attempts. 
 Shelton will eventually get his first win against the German but not today. I expect him to hold on for a while and we might see a tie-break, but I’ll still back Zverev to win in straight sets.
 My bet: Zverev to win in straight sets
